text: You sink your teeth into that first slice of square pizza pie from meta pizza-slinger Square Pie and triumphant victory is yours from the very first bite. The robust crackle of that exquisite Brooklyn square crust, the golden crunchy textures of next-level toasty caramelization evoked by the fermented yeast gods, and the ideal quantity of highest quality toppings. Couldn't decide between red sauce options of pepperoni cups or glistening, crumbly sausage morsels, so the solution to that problem was...spinach. Spinach wound up being most royally bomb. It was the right choice. The creamy mellowness of milky ricotta clouds dolloped with wild abandon (but not too recklessly) is positively dreamy, especially paired with the nutty saltiness of grana padano cheese, along with piles of tender, garlicky spinach. Drizzles of luscious herb oil create a blissful cohesion, pooling into tiny puddles and adding another sensational level of savory depth. And the garlic. This pie is beautifully ample on the garlic front, damn. If you can muster the restraint to save a couple of slices for later, do it. And then eat them after they've cooled down for awhile. My pizza gauge takes into account how good a slice is when eaten cold. It can't not. How does the slice taste at 5am the next day, or whenever desperation kicks in later? This is important. Then there's that ridiculous romaine salad on the menu, which includes fresh chopped romaine, a hard boiled egg, roasted tomatoes, artichokes, about a quarter pound of shredded sharp provolone, and a piquant red wine vinaigrette. It's unmistakably savory all the way through; delightfully briny and tangy and delicious, with satisfyingly on-point ratios. Rip open a piece of crust and shove some in it. The end.

text: I'm not the one to write a bad review, specially after being a server and bartender myself, but I have to say this was one of the worst experiences I've ever had. We arrived around 7:30 pm on a Sunday night. We had a party of 10 people (I knew we were gonna wait a while considering we didn't have a reservation) and we were not seated till after 9:00 pm. Because we were a lot of people they were seating us in two separate tables. Our party fortunately grew smaller so we only kept one table. A friend of ours recommended this place. We were visiting New Orleans for the first time. She said this was the best restaurant in New Orleans and that they had the best oysters. I'd never tried oysters before so I said I would give it a try. Our server, Claire, took a while to come to our table. As soon as she filled my glass of water and took my drink order, I asked for a dessert menu. Because it took an hour and a half to get a table I had a snack at the bar next door, which by the way had much better service than this restaurant. I wasn't very hungry, so I just wanted a dessert. It took a good 10 minutes before our drinks came out. Claire was about to start taking orders, and I asked her again for a dessert menu. She ran off like she was being chased and came back with the menu. She took everyone's order and finally came back around to me. I asked for the chocolate cake and specifically told her I wanted my dessert when everyone's food came out because I wanted to eat with everyone else. One of my guy friends had ordered another beer when he ordered his food but it never came out. He had to get up literally after his food came out and go up to the bar to get a beer (roughly about 30 minutes after he had ordered it). My fiancé asked for a chicken plate and ordered oysters as an appetizer. My friend also ordered the oysters as an appetizer. We waited for them to come out but our entrees came out before the appetizers. My friend, who'd ordered the oysters also had a soup, but to our surprise no one brought her a spoon. How was she supposed to eat her soup? With a fork? We finally found another server that was walking by and asked for a spoon. She said she would be back with one and completely forgot. So we grabbed another server and he brought her one. By then everyone was eating and we still didn't have the oysters, and I didn't have my dessert, so I was just eating off of my fiancé's plate. Claire came around with one order of oysters for my friend but not ours. My fiancé just said "don't worry about it, we'll try them another time". Besides he was getting full. Another one of my friends (who is vegetarian and had informed Claire about it) asked for a side of the whipped potatoes, and I asked if my dessert was coming. She said she was gonna go check on that. Later, the manager with the man bun, came around and asked if anyone had ordered an entree with whipped potatoes. No, we'd ordered just a side of whipped potatoes. Anyways, he informs Estefania that they were out, but he could replace it with a substitute that had crab in it. Umm, I thought we said she was vegetarian? He was like "yeah that wouldn't be fun." He then proceeded to ask if everything was okay. By this time everyone was done with their food (except Franchesca who was still working on her oysters that were supposed to be an appetizer), and I still didn't have my dessert. I asked him where it was and that I had asked for it to come out with everyone's food. He said they were barely working on it. What a shock. He cleared our table and dropped all the plates. (Sigh). After that was cleaned up, my dessert was finally there. I was the only one with a plate on the table now. I finished my dessert and Claire came back around. Not to our table though, to the table next to us. She kept her back towards us and wouldn't turn around even though we were calling her. As a server, I literally hate when people flag me down but we had no choice but to wave at her for her to even notice us. Being a server I know when a server is purposely ignoring their tables, and that's exactly what she was doing. We asked for the check. When she came back she was charging me for two drinks when I only had one. I then informed her that I was being charged for two drinks and goes "but you had two drinks." Ummm what? She went to our table three times throughout our entire experience, so when had I ordered that other drink? She then goes on to say "well who had two drinks?" No one, girl. Because you forgot about my friends beer! She had put one of my friend's drink in my tab. She then fixed it. Gave me back the check to sign but no pen. I'd never tipped less than 20% before but this was definitely not worthy of a tip. Of course we tipped accordingly but I feel like she didn't deserve it. I'm sure Claire is great server at some level, but not that night. She treated us like ignorant foreigners, and it showed. Definitely ruined our last night in New Orleans.
label: NEG

text: Natural Selection is one of my favorite stores in all of Midtown Reno. Just ask my boyfriend and he can confirm that I try to sneak a visit to this shop every time we pass by. Keep in mind that they don't open until noon, so plan your visit accordingly. Atmosphere: Walking in feels like stepping into the study of an old eccentric professor. From the ceiling hangs a variety of trailing indoor plants. The displays are filled with all manner of small complete animal skeletons, individual bones, and all kinds of other preserved animal parts (quills, teeth, alligator hands). Smaller house plants and succulents are tucked into every available corner, giving the whole shop a very wild overgrown feel to it. Animal Oddities: They have the best selection of animal bones, quills, skeletons, taxidermy, etc that I've ever seen in a shop in person. Every time I go back they have new specimens and new plants in stock. If you are interested they have a great Instagram page you can follow to stay up to date on all the new things coming in. Plants: I love how helpful the staff is here when buying a new plant. They are very knowledgeable on how to take care of each plant so that you have the best possible start.

text: Came to The Grand Sierra for New Year's. Went ice skating at the rink, and then to the buffet. We knew we would be waiting in line, but we had time to spare. 45 minutes later we reach the front. The cashier told me the total... $93 for two people on New year's. We looked up the price that morning and it was $31.99, guess they didn't change the website. We thought well we waited this long , let's just do it! Paid the total and left the tip. We get seated, our waiter was very busy , we didn't hold it against him but we're extremely thirsty. Finally got our drinks. Checked out all the food, decided on crab legs to start, we we're going to get our moneys worth! The crab was good, but it really stuck to the inside of the shell. After the crab I tried some other food... It was just ok. The sea food pasta wasn't that great and neither was the Walnut shrimp. I loaded up on fruit then decided I would fill myself up on dessert! I walked up and was immediately unimpressed. Little tiny cup sizes of everything , and what they had was lackluster, especially for the price of New year's ! I got a rice crispy treat, a vanilla flan and a little pecan pie. The rice crispy treats tasted like the fake ones you buy in store that aren't made with real marshmallow. The pecan pie was ok, but it was a lot of crust since it was tiny and not a lot of filling. The one thing I liked the best was the flan, that was delicious . Decided to go back and try once more, so I got an ice cream, spimoni, which I normally love. It just didn't taste right or was sweet enough. I don't know what they uses for the green and pink but it didn't taste like spimoni I ever had. The chocolate portion was very cocoa tasting. Overall , I would have given the buffet 3 stars. Was not very impressed given the price we paid , it was just a regular buffet, there was nothing special or out of the ordinary about that night. I would have gladly paid $25 for this buffet, but was not worth their inflated New Year's price of $45. BUT that's not all! The next day I checked my bank account to see the damage I had done the day before. I saw two charges from the Grand Buffet. One for the meal for two plus the tip and one for just the meal. They were both pending but the money had come out of my account. I called and they said sometimes it happens and the charge would most likely fall off in a day. Next day the payment posted. I didn't notice until 5:30 pm. Called and talked to someone else. The manager said there is nothing she can do without a receipt on her end and the call accounting but they were closed so I had to wait another day. Next day called accounting. The woman I talked to said their accounting team had already taken care of it, however it will be a few business days until my money is credited, which for me is very annoying to have $100 missing from my account for a week!

The bar/space is incredibly well done and sticks with their cabin theme. Easily my new favorite bar in the Speedway area. Easy parking in the street or small lot, there is a huge wraparound patio that can accommodate any sized group with a spacious beer garden in the building's rear. You enter the corner of Main & 10th under a large entrance with double doors. You are immediately greeted by a hostess station. The building is enormous, with high ceilings, and a massive bar in the center that is surrounded on all sides by dining booths/tables. Beyond the bar is another two rooms, a bar within a bar on the lower level and private parties on the upper level. The bar itself has a stone top with a wooden rail, a dark wooden bar face, and round dark steel footrest. I didn't count the bar stools, but I have to imagine 40-50 natural wood stools with black padded seats and rounded back support that stick with the outdoor/cabin theme surround the bar on all sides. Small, but I'm sure, not cheap, details that really make the place feel comfortable. The bar's center contains all the taps, Hard Truth and other spirits, and several large HDTVs that make Big Woods an ideal place to watch the big game. The food is delicious. I've tried so many items on the menu. I have taken several friends, no one ever complains about the taste or the portion size. And finally, the beers. The six-foot blonde is one of my favorite craft beers period, out of any/all of the breweries I've visited. They have a sizable beer menu that will provide any beer drinker something they like. The Quaff On Brewing Company is killing it, and the owners pay attention to the details. Big Woods in Speedway is incredible, and I look forward to my next visit.

text: I came for David Bowie art and discovered a museum that had much more than I expected! When Philly Loves Bowie Week hosts their annual events I always make a point to at least go and enjoy their amazing art exhibit that goes on display. So when I learned that they were moving it to National Liberty Museum this year, and that they were going to have it on display for a full month, I decided to make a day visit out of it. And when I did I realized that the full museum featured so much more than just the kitschy never forget 9/11 things that I was expecting. Liberty is one of those subjective words that can be linked to anything from religion and science, to heroism and inspiration, to anywhere in between. And I was pleasantly surprised to see a little bit of all of those things represented within the museums confines. Outside of the obvious Bowie exhibit, I was also very won over by the wall of inspirational heroes who made an impact despite facing physical and cognitive disabilities. Another incredible room was. The Heroes From Around The World room is also noteworthy for paying homage to noteworthy people like Nelson Mandela and Anne Frank, and featuring a breathtaking Flame of Liberty installation from world renowned glass artist, Dale Chihuly. While the Bowie exhibit is long gone it gave a wonderful showing of what the museums special exhibits had to feature, while offering up some things that the previous years Bowie art installations didn't, like art from elementary and middle school students who were newly exposed to his music. While it may also invoke a grain of sadness, the latest special exhibit, Forbidden Art from the collections of the Auschwitz Memorial, may very well do the same during a time when its needed to.

text: I was not compensated in any way for my review. I spent a lot of time researching and trying Reno buffets in the last month, and I have to say hands down, Toucan Charlie's is by far the epitome of grand design and excellent eats. I had the wonderful opportunity to meet with Atlantis's Communications Manager Laura, and Corporate Executive Chef Robert to learn about the operations! Toucan Charlie's serves on average ten thousand guests per week which translates to more than a half a million guests per year. Each day guests consume 13-18 prime ribs which by the way is also served at lunchtime, guests also indulge in several tons of the delicious gelato they have in the Dessert Island. The most popular item is Pupusas served on Thursday and Friday and for vegetarians, the Veggie Benedict and braised tofu is sure to please your palette. Yes, there are vegetarian and gluten free options, so bring your appetite. So, my experience ... Let's start with design the interior is large, warm, modern and great for groups or a solo diner. There is no bad seat in this restaurant and warm plates are accessible from multiple locations. Also, for those of us who like to have clean hands, there are hand sanitizing stations on both sides of the buffet. The salad bar has to be the most extensive I have yet to see in Reno. This Buffet is massive, and I feel like I am in Las Vegas which is exactly what I was looking for. You can tell the quality of a buffet when they have beautifully placed hand-carved food artwork, it's a sign of experienced seasoned culinary professionals. You can tell there is a lot of passion in this kitchen. In the words of Virginia Wolf "One cannot think well, love well, sleep well, if one has not dined well." Nothing could have been more correct, upon first bite I began to think very well, it was clear that I was going to have a love affair here at Toucan Charlie's, and boy did I. I tasted each item individually, which makes it easy to judge everything, but hard to not need to let out a few notches on the belt. Hands down, the meats at the carvery are of the highest quality and the flavors I experienced are unrivaled in perfection. I tried the Pho, (MmM Delicious) I had a made to order salad, (NomNomNom) I also had made to order pesto pasta with shrimp and that was mouthwatering. The bagels and lox was even delicious and I'm not a B&L guy. You know how most buffet egg rolls are dry, crunchy and usually tasteless? That was not the case, for once I actually enjoyed a buffet egg roll. In fact without a doubt, the only two items I didn't like were the fried chicken and the baked chicken. I ate and ate and ate and all was good. And then, like a siren at sea, the Dessert Island called me over and I began my final phase of this extensive delicious research. The chocolate mouse cake melted in my mouth, the rice pudding, the cotton candy, and the Gelato, I'll never forget the Gelato (blows dessert island a kiss ,, I'll see you again very soon desert island 3) Let's not forget the service. My water glass never went empty , and my plates were cleared as quickly as I could go back for more. I loved how the place was full but did not feel packed, every seat is a good seat and every dish is a great choice By far, my best Reno Buffet experience.

text: We used to go to Chez Elena Wu in Voorhees, but when we moved to Moorestown, this is closer to us, and the owners are the same. Having been here a number of times, I feel embarrassed to have not reviewed it, since we always enjoy it so much. Most recently, my Husband and I were starving when we got there, so we totally went to town with our ordering. We were pleasantly greeted and seated right away. Our server acknowledged us within a minute or so, and asked how many wine glasses we would like (they are BYOB, which is really nice on the budget), and we were brought glasses of water. Started with dumplings and honey glazed spare ribs to share - both were so delicious. I have to admit that I like very thin skins on my dumplings, and the skins are a little on the thicker side, but not as much as most Chinese take-out places (I do not consider this to be a standard Chinese take-out, by any means). The slightly sweet ribs were perfectly seasoned. My husband also ordered soup, which he loved, but I cannot remember what he ordered. He suggested that we split an order of the Honey Walnut Shrimp, which we have previously had, both here, and at Chez Elena Wu; I told him I would not ever share this delightful dish, after looking at him as if he had gone stark raving mad! This is one of the most wonderful meals, and it has ALWAYS been made to perfection. I have tried several other entrees, but each time, I wish I had gone back to my HW Shrimp. Not that the other dishes weren't delicious, but this one is perfection. Service has always been pleasant, and efficient enough that I have no complaints. The prices are very good, especially when you are not paying the mark up on alcohol. I truly recommend Très Yan and Wu! The restaurant is in a strip mall, but the interior is very pleasant, and you cannot see the parking area through the window treatments, so all that matters is the food and ambience....

text: My husband needed surgery to remove a disk and fuse two vertebrae in his neck. The pain has been so bad that he was looking forward to getting this done so he'd have relief. My review is based on what we consider to be really lousy service. It hasn't been long enough to evaluate how successful his outcome will be, but we are well aware of the lack of customer service provided so far. First, a few months ago he was scheduled for an appointment and received a reminder the day before. He confirmed and showed up 15 minutes early. When he approached the front desk he was told he had no appointment scheduled. Not that day, not any day, not at any location. When he was obviously surprised and asked if that's the case why had he received a reminder the day before the response was a shrug of the shoulders. Next issue: he had all of his pre-op tests and X-rays done, at CTMC as ordered. He was then called and told to come in to the large Downtown Reno Renown campus for further pre-op work. We live in Gardnerville, and CTMC is far enough but Renown in Reno is a significant distance (about 45 minutes). That's where the procedure was scheduled to happen so he went. They re-did everything that had been done at CTMC. Why? He asked, and nobody could tell him. That means that his insurance will be billed twice for identical testing and then of course he'll be billed for whatever copayment is due - twice. Next, surgery is performed on time and I will say that the surgical suite is very nice. Very efficient and well run. I loved getting text updates that told me where he was every step of the way. Even the overnight stay and discharge procedures were efficient. Here's where the big problems arise. He's given 3 prescriptions. One for antibiotics, one for muscle relaxers, and one for pain relief. The instructions on the pain pills say "take one OR two every xx hours for 7 days. Taking one pill did nothing for him so the next time he took 2. He was very careful to not take them more frequently than ordered even though the pain was intense, and the medication wore off at least an hour before the next dose. Since he had to take 2, he realized that he was going to run out after 4 days. His surgery was on a Tuesday, so that meant he'd run out over the weekend if he continued to take 2 as ordered. So he resorted to taking 1 and then the next dose taking 2, trying to make sure he'd get through the weekend and hoping he wouldn't need them any longer. On Monday morning, 6 days post-op, he called the surgeon's office to inquire about what to do. He let them know that the pain was off the charts, and that he only had 2 pills left. I was on call ready to go pick it up for him since there's no way he'd be able to drive 45 miles to Reno with his pain level so bad. Nobody called him back, despite him leaving the message first thing Monday morning and conveying how much pain he was in. I asked him if he wanted me to take him into urgent care or emergency and of course he declined that offer, primarily because of how much such a visit would end up costing. He also said if he's going to be in this much pain he'd much rather be in his home rather than a waiting room chair. He's going to have a really tough night and likely end up taking more Tylenol than is recommended to try to stay somewhat comfortable. As for Dr Lynch, when he was talking to me after surgery he said not once, not twice, but three times how "he's a big guy" while he was describing what he'd done during the procedure. No shit Sherlock. Not anything we didn't know, not anything he didn't know prior to surgery. Granted, all of my husband's pre-op visits were with a PA and he'd only seen Dr Lynch once prior to surgery for about 5 minutes. But why is it necessary to keep repeating such a statement to concerned family right after coming out of surgery? I found it insulting. My husband carries an extra 50 pounds - so what? Most everyone carries around some extra weight. Even Dr Lynch! Finally, my friend who is scheduled to have this very same procedure a week from today called her surgeon's office today, concerned about how much pain she'll be in afterward. She has a different provider but her surgery will be in the same place as my husband's surgery. The PA she spoke with said "let me guess, your friend's procedure was performed by Dr Lynch from Spine Nevada?" She said yes, and asked how she knew that. She said Dr Lynch's patients always experience more pain and have a more difficult recovery because he's not as careful during such a delicate procedure. Seeing the level of pain my husband is suffering and the callous comments post-op, combined with a scheduling screw up that cost us a full day and now no response to calls about pain relief, if I ever need surgery and am referred to Nevada Spine I'll ask for a different referral.

text: Bottom line: don't rent here. I should have looked more. I was new to STL and take internet reviews with a grain of salt- but the negative reviews of Trilogy are true. I *promise* you can find something better for the same price. Keep looking. First, Trilogy was reluctant to show me the unit I would actually be renting. I asked multiple times but was only shown the model until the day I signed, which made me feel rushed after losing out on other options while waiting to see the unit (no one was occupying the unit when I was beginning this process, so it was empty and viewable). The apartment I ended up with is remarkably different than the model. While they take care to a make the model presentable, they do the bare minimum to even keep the actual units livable. Second, upon move-in, I was met with a host of issues. 1) a pool of dirty water in the bottom of the dysfunctional dishwasher 2) a streak of blood on the bathroom door 3) a baby cockroach in the kitchen cabinets 4) a stove with only one working burner 5) grimy, disgusting blinds 6) food crumbs inside kitchen storage left from the previous tenant. There are abandoned, rusted bikes in the yard and the dumpsters are overflowing with waste. Come November, I learned the hard way that my heat also wasn't working. If you scroll past all the positive reviews they probably had someone write, you'll see that the issues are frequent here. *Also, they simply sprayed for cockroaches. Baby cockroaches are signs of an infestation, and spraying doesn't make them go away. I had frequent issues with their rent portal telling me I owed more money than I actually did- a constant stressor, 3/4 months I lived there, as I did not want to be overcharged or accused of not paying. And, in response to this understandably urgent concern, I rarely received a timely email or call without feeling as if I had to hassle the office. I was unhappy with my decision to live here within the month. I reached out to the office to ask about my options (subletting, transferring the lease, breaking the lease, etc). I was first told that subletting is not an option, and that I could sign on a roommate and leave the premises but that I would still have to keep my name on the lease. I later reached back out to clarify whether or not there was any way to remove myself from the lease, because my circumstances changed. I was then informed that if I found someone to add as a roommate, I could be removed from the lease so the lease would essentially become theirs and I could move on. I clarified this multiple times via email in writing. After sending multiple prospective in to apply for the unit and after receiving no communication in return from the office, I called one day to find out that I had been given false information. I spent months looking for a new tenant, showing my apartment, and finding a new place to be met with no options after being told by one of their employees *in writing* that I could sign over my lease to another individual. Even with proof of what I was told, the office would not allow me to have a new individual apply in order to remove my name. They insist they don't allow subletting (though in the lease it just says not permitted without *written permission* - I'm fairly certain its illegal to bar subletting without reasonable justification). Ultimately they waived paying back the concessions I received upon move in if I chose to break my lease, but after months of planning, I had to decide whether to pay upwards of $3000 to break my lease or to stay and remain unhappy. This place is so dilapidated and unprofessional, I chose to pay thousands to leave. To add insult to injury, the office staff is, indeed, unprofessional. And I generally refrain from saying so because it's easy to get frustrated as a tenant. However, communication is poor and next to none. While I did become difficult when dealing with the above issue (but I believe rightfully so) - I was questioned as to why I needed clarification and why I asked so many questions about my lease in the first place. Tenants should be able to ask as many questions as needed. This was their error, not my own. Lastly, when you view the apartments they tell you that water, sewer, trash is included, but when you sign the lease you find out this is tacked on to the rent. So, my unit listed as $850 is actually $900. Like I said, you can find better elsewhere. Ultimately, I deeply regret signing here and hope that this negative review is positive in that it helps others avoid these old, dilapidated apartments and frustrating apartment company.

text: This is the worst customer experience I've ever had with any business. I feel that consumers should be able to make informed decisions about how they spend their money, and when I had a problem with my car, unfortunately, I trusted Dowdy's to provide an accurate diagnosis based on the symptoms I described. However, Dowdy's Automotive wrote up a document that stated that the issue I described was an oil leak, when it was not. But, because I signed their inaccurate document accepting service for an oil leak, I now have no recourse for the situation I'm about to describe. The sickening part is that the Vice President of the company seems delighted about being able to keep my money knowing that there's nothing I can do about it. I say that due to his comments during a nasty phone call that he made to me which I will describe below: My car was leaking all over the garage, so I agreed to have it fixed by Dowdy's for $1381. They said it was an oil leak. When I finally got the car back an entire week later, I noticed the car was still leaking. I gave it back to them for another week. They said the car was not leaking, but when I got the car back home the 2nd time, I immediately noticed that it was still leaking. Having been without my car for two weeks, I am understandably fed up and just want a refund. The unsympathetic and argumentative shop manager, Brandon, was bad enough, but it got worse when he gave my number to what turned out to be the company's very belligerent Vice President. The VP called me while I was at school. I told him that I didn't have a ton of time to be on the phone, and that I needed a quick answer from him about the refund. Instead of being extremely sorry for the situation, the inconvenience, and lack of trust that I now feel towards them, the VP was focused on me leaving an online review about my experience. My conversation with him was seriously shocking. He constantly interrupted me, and, at first he said that he was "not inclined to continue to work with me if I was going to leave a negative review." So, I questioned him and asked him if he was saying that he was not going to honor the warranty, because I wrote a review. He then realized that what he had said was not only inconsistent with his company's warranty, but also a violation of the consumer protection act, so he started to change his position and, he said, "incase the call was being recorded". He then said that he was "not going to go above and beyond" for someone who leaves a negative review while simultaneously refusing to give them a 3rd chance to fix the problem. Not going above and beyond under these circumstances is my definition of providing worse customer service than prior to his nasty phone call to me. As previously mentioned, they had a 2nd chance and an extra week to fix the problem. They had plenty of time to see the car leaking, but weren't thorough enough to figure things out. Anyway, I told him on the phone that, at this point, I felt they were incompetent and that I was going to now have the dealer diagnose my car. I was not surprised to find out from the dealer that the leak that I had originally described to Dowdy's was not the source of fluid on my garage floor. It was a power steering fluid leak. So, here I've been over two weeks without my car and charged $1381 to fix what had to have been a tiny oil leak. (Who knows if there even was an oil leak.) Even though Dowdy's misdiagnosed the problem that I described to them as an oil leak when it was not, they still REFUSED to refund my $1381 because I "signed the paperwork" and agreed to an oil leak repair. That is seriously messed up. They decided to return only $300 and fixed the power steering for free, without providing a warranty on the power steering. Absolutely terrible "goodwill". In the end, I've spent $960 more than I needed to spend because the power steering was only going to cost $340 at the dealer. I finally had to agree to their bogus offer because I needed my car back in working order. It has been extremely inconvenient to not have my car for so long and I have little faith that this latest work will hold up given that there is no warranty. The VP has since sent an email in an attempt to redeem himself and his company from his angry and aggressive behavior and his company's lack of thoroughness and also to have his final position "on the record." (Which is another indication of how nasty he was on the phone). Regarding the negative review, he writes: "What I didn't understand and what I tried to convey is why you would try to work with us on one side and drag us through the mud on the other side even before we had a chance to resolve the problem." (Really? You've had 2 weeks.) He also apologizes for "his part" in escalating the conversation. Well, "his part" was freak show insane. Neither his email, nor the final and best offer to correct the situation redeems them in my eyes when they are keeping $960 of my dollars.

For a company which makes this statement on their website: "It's all about the customer, not the product," Mr. Gerhard said in 1957, "We don't sell appliances. We sell customer service. For restaurant week, I had their veggie samosas and butter chicken - also SO delicious and perfectly done. In addition to how perfectly IndeBlue executes its dishes, the service is extraordinary as well. It's not often that you happen upon both in one place!!! The service we had for restaurant week was some of the best I've seen in the city - the manager politely stopped by to check and see how we were doing, AND the server comp'ed us some turmeric chai tea lattes for our walk home to warm us up. I cannot sing enough praise about IndeBlue, it's one of our favourite restaurants in the city whenever we are craving something reliably good. Highly, HIGHLY recommend.

If anything, it was a bland dish that is not worth it. I did sample a few other dishes from my table. The lemon ricotta pancakes, blueberry pancakes, and a special B.E.C Sandwich on a "Philly Bun" were all solid. No one found anything that was a must have. Overall, solid brunch spot with some tasty brunch dishes. Service and the vibe are what bring it from a 3 to a 4.

text: The day before Thanksgiving my family decided to check out the recently opened Harps of Trinity Irish Pub and Grill and we certainly were not disappointed. From the minute we walked in the door we were impressed by how warm and inviting this new hot spot looked. Kudos to Wendy for the beautiful decorating! There are those little touches that impress such as a carafe of water and glasses for patrons who are just seated. There is a mix of high-top and low tables which are nicely buffered by well-placed planters. We were happy to see some familiar faces like owner Vince La Mattina and our favorite bartender Taylor. Manager Masahiko also stopped by as he made his rounds to ensure everyone was being well taken care of. Our waiter Hunter was knowledgeable and attentive but allowed us to relax and enjoy our experience which we absolutely did. Thanks for excellent service Hunter! The vibe of Harps was impressive but the true star of the night was the amazing cuisine prepared by Chef Rob and his incredibly talented kitchen staff. Our daughter ordered the Fish and Chips which we all had to try. The fish was properly battered and crisp on the outside yet tender and moist on the inside. It was obvious the fries were fresh cut and again, cooked perfectly. This was also accompanied by a tasty homemade coleslaw and is a dish I would certainly recommend. My wife and I decided to try the entrée special that night which was Grilled Mahi Mahi with Shishito Coconut Rice, house veggies and green coconut sauce. We were both impressed on how beautifully the food was arranged on our plates. The Mahi was grilled to perfection and extremely tasty and moist. The shishito coconut rice was bursting with flavor and was the perfect accompaniment for the fish as was the green coconut sauce for dipping. This was paired with a mélange of delicious roasted and seasoned zucchini, yellow squash, sweet red onions and red bell pepper. And if that was not enough the fish was topped with tempura asparagus. Wow! The flavor profiles all played together nicely and when paired with The Other West Coast IPA from local Trinity brewer The Escape Brewing Company. Truly an impressive meal! Harps menu has a nice variety of appetizers, salads and entrees to please all palates. They also have live music on the weekend but even on this Wednesday night they had a DJ coming in at 9pm to kick off the Thanksgiving holiday. Harps is a welcome addition to the Trinity area and one I am sure many will come to enjoy now and in the future.

text: A classic authentic Korean restaurant. My husband was in Korea for over a year and I went for 3 weeks. Parking: plenty in the parking lot Interior and atmosphere: typical Korean style. Minimalist. Quiet. Great place for kids, families and couples. Service: great! Hang with me here...Korean service is very simple. They greet you, wait a bit, take your order and leave you alone, then bring the banchan (like tapas), leave you alone, bring the meal and leave you alone. They believe in letting the customers eat, drink and talk and not be interrupted by service. Every place in Korea does this and this place is no exception. You need something grab their attention, simple. They keep an eye out for you quietly from a far, trust me they are watching to see if you need something. Remember in Korea it's about food, drink, family and socializing not the service. Food: great lunch specials and tons of traditional options. Vegans and vegetarians can be accommodated by asking. They will show you all the options available. Korean food has zero dairy so really everything would be made vegan. One of the banchan has egg, the rest are vegan. The beef stew (pictured) comes with scissors. Yes. Scissors to cut the meat off the bone. That is authentic folks. If you understand the culture of Korea then you will enjoy yourself here and love the food OR if you are open to new cultural food experiences you will have a great visit to Korea!

text: Going to SOS feels like going to my mom's house. The food is comforting and homey-feeling. The interior may not reflect the homeyness, but the food is good. Lunch orders are reasonably priced and comes with a side of rice and four sides. I recommend ordering ahead since lunch gets busy there. 3. If you want to try authentic Korean, try the soups. It's what I'm used to eating at home. A great start for newbies is the Yookgaejang or Soondubu. They are spicy and packs a lot of flavor. The seollungtang is subtle bone broth that may be harder to please the masses. You'll have to season the soup with salt and pepper. 4. SOS also offers homemade kimchi and side dishes to-go. These items are made daily in-house. You can usually find these items at the local Asian markets too. Great Korean place that I hope to see succeed. It hides in the sea of restaurants off Page but is located close to Sonic. I wish you the best SOS! I am looking forward to many future meals here and bringing friends.

My favorite has a few layers of the mix soft serve, toasted rice, sweet azuki bean (red bean) paste + mochi balls. Mmm so good! My go to drink is the Black Sesame Matcha latte. Such a great combo! They have soy milk for their lattes if you are lactose intolerant. The staff are very friendly and always helpful to explain anything from the menu. If you are new to matcha and want their soft serve, start with the vanilla/matcha mix, all matcha may be too strong to start with off the bat. They have a cute little tatami room for bigger groups where you need to take off your shoes to sit inside. Earlier this year, they opened their patio so you can enjoy the sun!

text: If it were possible to give this company a 1/2 star rating I would do it, maybe a ¼ star. Home Depot set all this up. On September 28, 2019 my stackable washer dryer was to be delivered. I told them I didn't know which water supply spicket was hot and which was cold. I told them I would hook up a hose to determine that. When I was unhooking the hose one guy said now you can hook-up your supply line to the water supply spickets. I wondered why he would say this, but thought that maybe they aren't allowed to hook the hoses up to my water line. I hooked it up. I then fed him the water lines to hook-up to the machine. He knew I had new 6 foot new hoses, exhaust line, and a 6 foot pigtail in the original packages. When he hooked up the system he handed the plugs out to the garage and said you can hook these up. I told him they would not reach. He then came out and pulled them through and hooked them up. I suspect if I had hooked up the electrical and anything was wrong with the machine they would not have stood behind it. He turned on the machines and ran them for about three minutes. They said wait until I hear from them and if I do not get back in touch with them. When I told the HD employee the story he said I don't believe you. I then called the dispatcher again. The dispatcher contacted the installers and I was told they will not return because I hooked-up the water. All they did was hook up the exhaust line. I explained that was not true. She said, "why didn't you tell them no." I explained I didn't know to do that and thought this was customary. I talked to her about a half hour and hung up. A buddy came over to help me. The steam-cleaning water line behind the washer was loose. We tightened it and the water leak stopped. Then I realized they had not used a new exhaust line to hook-up the exhaust. They just hooked-up my old line. They did that poorly and it was very loose. I went to Home Depot and they were very good about things and returned my money for the unused parts. They only used the pigtail off the truck. Before buying appliances from HD and if you live in FL you better ask if Ralph's Appliance Transport Company and of it is be prepared for trouble.
